prompt:
Build a physically causal aircraft fuel-supply system with left and right wing tanks, a center tank, two independently commanded transfer pumps on each wing, one-way protection between parallel pump branches, controlled tank isolation, and a center-tank feed path with an engine-side pump and demand. Fuel must move through the physical hydraulic network; the model must not prescribe tank volumes or engine delivery directly.

Read flight_fuel_command and initial_fuel_volume_m3 from the MATLAB base workspace. flight_fuel_command is a six-channel Timeseries containing [left fuel-line elevation, right fuel-line elevation, left upper pump speed, left lower pump speed, right upper pump speed, right lower pump speed] in [m, m, rev/s, rev/s, rev/s, rev/s]. Support fuel-line elevations from -1 to 1 m and pump commands from 0 to 120 rev/s. initial_fuel_volume_m3 contains [fuel in each wing tank, fuel in the center tank] and must support 8 to 11.5 m^3 in each wing tank and 4 to 8 m^3 in the center tank.

Regulate each transfer pump's measured shaft speed in closed loop. The system must continue supplying the engine through single-pump and asymmetric pump-command disturbances, prevent sustained reverse transfer through an unavailable branch, protect tanks against dry-out and overflow, and remain physically bounded during fuel-line elevation changes. Changes in pump commands and line elevation must propagate through pump speed, pressure rise, transfer flow, tank inventory, and engine delivery.

Log five MATLAB Timeseries named pump_speed_state, tank_fuel_state, transfer_hydraulics, engine_feed_state, and pump_power_state for the complete simulation interval. pump_speed_state has 8 channels in this order: command and measured speed for left-upper, left-lower, right-upper, and right-lower pumps, all in rpm. tank_fuel_state has 4 channels: left-, right-, and center-tank volume (m^3), then lateral fuel-CG offset (percent). transfer_hydraulics has 8 channels: the four pump mass flows (kg/s) followed by their four pressure rises (MPa), in the same pump order. engine_feed_state has 2 channels: engine-feed mass flow (kg/s) and engine-pump pressure rise (MPa). pump_power_state has 8 channels: the four shaft powers followed by the four hydraulic powers, all in W and in the same pump order. All logged quantities must be measured from the same causal physical simulation.

Save the completed model as cand_XFLUID08.slx in the submission directory and keep the latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XFLUID08.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
